topic: the physiological blind spot and perceptual filling-in

continuity_bible.subject_identity: the same adult viewer represented only by one hazel human eye and one consistent clean anatomical eye model
continuity_bible.environment: dark charcoal science studio with a single warm practical reflection and restrained teal optical graphics
continuity_bible.lighting: soft key from camera left, narrow warm rim from camera right, black-to-charcoal background
continuity_bible.color_treatment: photoreal neutral skin and eye color, deep charcoal, restrained teal signal paths, amber payoff accent
continuity_bible.screen_direction: visual information travels left-to-right toward the optic nerve and brain
continuity_bible.camera_language: macro optics, precise slow pushes, motivated transitions through the pupil, no handheld shake

factual_notes.claim: Photoreceptors in the retina convert light into electrical signals that travel through the optic nerve to the brain.
factual_notes.source_title: How the Eyes Work — National Eye Institute

factual_notes.claim: The physiological blind spot corresponds to the location where the optic nerve exits and visual cells are absent.
factual_notes.source_title: National Eye Institute glossary — blind spot

factual_notes.claim: Perceptual filling-in can make the visual system fill the informational void at the blind spot using surrounding content.
factual_notes.source_title: Predictive Coding: A Possible Explanation of Filling-In at the Blind Spot

source_phrases_for_originality_check: photoreceptors turn the light into electrical signals
the visual system fills the informational void

script_segments.narration: There is a hole in your vision right now, and you almost never notice it.
script_segments.caption: A HOLE IN YOUR VISION
script_segments.visual_action: Extreme macro of the same hazel eye opening; a tiny circular region of the reflected scene vanishes without a glitch effect
script_segments.entry_action: Begin on black and reveal the eye with one natural blink
script_segments.exit_action: End pushing directly toward the pupil while the missing region stays visually stable
script_segments.camera: 100mm macro, slow centered push toward pupil

script_segments.narration: Inside each eye, light lands on a retina packed with cells that detect it.
script_segments.caption: LIGHT → RETINA
script_segments.visual_action: Seamless travel through the pupil into the same anatomically clean eye model as focused light reaches the curved retina
script_segments.entry_action: Continue the forward movement through the pupil from shot one
script_segments.exit_action: Follow one teal signal left-to-right across the retina
script_segments.camera: Controlled macro fly-through, medically plausible proportions
script_segments.ambience: Same optical-room hum with a faint electrical texture

script_segments.narration: But one small spot has no visual cells at all.
script_segments.caption: NO VISUAL CELLS HERE
script_segments.visual_action: The retinal surface reveals one small optic-disc region without photoreceptor markers while surrounding cells remain dense
script_segments.entry_action: Enter following the same teal signal across the retina
script_segments.exit_action: Signal curves toward the optic nerve opening at frame right
script_segments.camera: Slow lateral macro track across retinal surface
script_segments.ambience: Continuous hum; electrical texture briefly thins
script_segments.sfx: Subtle low drop when the empty region appears

script_segments.narration: That is where the optic nerve leaves the eye, carrying signals toward the brain.
script_segments.caption: THE OPTIC NERVE EXIT
script_segments.visual_action: Same eye model rotates slightly as signal paths converge and leave through the optic nerve toward an abstract brain silhouette
script_segments.entry_action: Continue the signal movement from the optic-disc region
script_segments.exit_action: End with the signal exiting frame right toward the brain
script_segments.camera: Measured pullback from retina to eye-and-nerve profile
script_segments.ambience: Hum continues with gentle neural pulses

script_segments.narration: Close one eye during a dot test, and the missing mark can disappear completely.
script_segments.caption: TRY THE DOT TEST
script_segments.visual_action: Minimal original dot-and-cross demonstration in the same charcoal studio; the dot naturally disappears at one viewing position
script_segments.entry_action: Brain-bound signal becomes the horizontal test line
script_segments.exit_action: Hold briefly after the dot disappears, then begin restoring the surrounding pattern
script_segments.camera: Locked perpendicular demonstration view with a subtle controlled push
script_segments.ambience: Continuous hum with space left for narration
script_segments.sfx: Quiet disappearance tick, no digital glitch

script_segments.narration: Your brain fills the gap from the surrounding pattern. Seeing is partly reconstruction.
script_segments.caption: SEEING IS RECONSTRUCTION
script_segments.visual_action: Return to the same hazel eye as the surrounding studio reflection flows smoothly across the blind-spot region; restrained amber highlight marks the reveal
script_segments.entry_action: The test pattern flows into the reflection on the eye
script_segments.exit_action: End on a steady eye with the complete reflection and a clean half-second hold
script_segments.camera: Slow pull back from macro eye to a composed final close-up
script_segments.ambience: Hum resolves into a warm sustained tone
